evidence.criterion: O1: Cases A, B, and C are all rerun after the edit rather than retesting only B.

evidence.citation: “using fresh, context-free blind runners, one agent per case per run” and “A separate fresh judge graded each artifact” establish fresh runners and separate judges.
evidence.criterion: O2: Each repeated trial uses a fresh blind runner per case and a separate evidence-based judge.

evidence.criterion: O3: Important cases receive enough repetitions to report per-case pass rates and expose nondeterministic regressions.

evidence.criterion: O4: A new miss is diagnosed as a skill defect versus a bad case before another revision, and the diagnose-revise-full-sweep loop repeats as needed.

human_labels.judge_rationale: The artifact correctly requires a fresh, blind, independently judged full-suite rerun with repetitions and per-case rates, and it prevents declaring success without regression checks. It does not, however, require classifying subsequent misses as skill defects versus bad cases and iterating the diagnose-revise-full-sweep loop, nor does it explicitly require a before-and-after comparison with cited gaps.

observations.value:
Re-evaluate all cases—A, B, and C—not only B—using fresh, context-free blind runners, one agent per case per run.

Before declaring success, show:

- Each runner saw only its case input and the target skill, never the bar or expected output.
- A separate fresh judge graded each artifact against that case’s bar and the skill’s first principles, citing specific artifact evidence for every verdict.
- B now passes consistently across 2–3 blind reruns, with its pass rate reported.
- A and C still pass, demonstrating the B-specific edit caused no regressions; rerun borderline or important cases 2–3 times and report their pass rates too.
- The live checkout was checked after every run and any leaked changes were cleaned.

The fix worked only when every case clears its required rate bar—not merely when B produces one passing run.
